title: Before the Storm
text:
The afternoon turned strange before the rain arrived. The air grew heavy and still, the birds fell silent, and the light took on a curious greenish colour that made the flats look like a photograph.
Uncle Rahman, who had fished these waters for forty years, glanced at the sky and began hauling his nets in without a word. The younger men laughed at him. The sun, they said, was still shining.
Twenty minutes later the wind arrived, flattening the sea into white streaks and tearing an umbrella clean off its pole. The younger men ran for shelter, soaked and shouting. Uncle Rahman was already home, drinking his tea, listening to the rain hammer on the roof.
